rationale: Replace find_frame's per-id glob over frames/*/<id>.jsonl with one process-local id -> path table guarded on every lookup by a complete {date_dir_name: st_mtime_ns} map from os.scandir(frames_root). Any directory-name or mtime difference rebuilds the table. T1 is strict: a returned path must be a live match for that id at return time. T2 is strict and measurable: when a stat issued after a foreign creation can observe the directory mtime change, the guard must rebuild and duplicate live ids must raise RuntimeError. The prior three obligations remain: a vanished indexed path falls back to glob, any append under frames/ in this process invalidates the table, and multiple live matches still raise. The residual is explicit and is not a rollback trigger: a foreign creation within the same roughly 1 ms directory-mtime tick as the guard observation can remain invisible for that lookup. The supporting probe observed 197/200 creation-time mtime changes, 3/200 unchanged, and a 0.9921 ms smallest positive delta (proposals/find-frame-index-v0.1/_probe_20260801_guard_cost_and_mtime.out.json). On the revised frozen candidate fb16689a63538f39d35374a123c860c0bfbfddeca900fd10027483c865830996, four interleaved lineage-show runs over 5887 records produced byte-identical stdout: baseline 32.155 s and 35.056 s; candidate 12.821 s and 12.928 s; minimum-run speedup 2.51x and mean-ratio speedup 2.61x.
rollback_triggers: candidate changes any file outside the two declared candidate paths
T1: find_frame returns a path that is not a live match for that id at the return time
T2: after a foreign creation, a subsequent stat can observe the directory mtime change but the guard does not rebuild and lookup does not raise RuntimeError for duplicate live ids
a frame opened by the running process becomes invisible to a later lookup in that process
